responsibility: This module provides the Rust frontend’s shared utility and support layer: reusable containers and compatibility abstractions such as optional/expected, buffering, bidirectional maps, identifier interning, and common enums; frontend-wide language metadata for ABIs, editions, operators, keywords, builtin attributes, and compiler-recognized lang items; and the core cross-cutting mapping infrastructure that assigns and queries crate, node, HIR, and definition identities, canonical paths, module relationships, visibility, macros, and language items across AST and HIR. It also contains text and token support that is specific to Rust source handling, including Unicode code point and UTF-8 utilities, generated normalization/property tables, punycode and base62 encoding, path-segment unwrapping, module file ownership rules, and conversion between lexer tokens and procedural-macro token streams. Overall, gcc/rust/util is the common substrate that other Rust frontend stages depend on for stable naming, metadata lookup, source-text handling, diagnostics-friendly identity tracking, and small infrastructural helpers rather than for parsing, type checking, or code generation themselves.
